Reticle Ranging Formulas - Calculating the distance to target using your scope reticle

Lots of different formulas there, but you only need to learn the one for your own scope's reticle (MRAD, MOA or IPHY).

Things you need to know for these formulas to work: the reticle type you have and what those markings on it mean, and the estimated height of the target.

I would recommend getting a scope with the MRAD reticle, which has easy to remember formula (and clicks are easy to understand too, 1 click at 100 meters is 1 cm). You might even be able to do the math in your head, without the need of pen and paper or calculator.

Using First Focal Plane scope is easier, since the reticle measurements always stay the same. With Second Focal Plane scope, the measurements change with different magnifications. Scope manual tells you what the measurements for each of the lines are. My scope for example is Second Focal Plane, Sightron S-Tac 2.5-17.5x56 http://sightronusa.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/Mil-HashIll_wDims-300x300.jpg the "A" measurement is 10 mils on the max 17.5 magnifications and 70 mils on the min 2.5 magnification and the "F" is 1 mil on max and 7 mils on min. Might not be so easy with SFP scope, manual with those measurements might come in handy or just remember to keep it on the right magnifications where you know the markings are right.

MRAD calculation examples:

Your average guy is 1.75 meters or so and he is 3.5 mrads on your reticle

1.75/3.5x1000=500 meters

or you are shooting a plate which is 0.45 meters high and it is 0.5 mrads on your reticle

0,45/0,5*1000=900 meters (this you could even calculate in your head)

or you are facing a Russian T-72 tank head on, part of the crew happily sitting on top of it. You check Wikipedia or some manual for tank dimensions. Width is easy to measure head on, if it would be on an angle towards you, you would have to pick height for example. T-72 width is 3.59 meters and it is 9 mrads on your reticle.

3.59/9*1000=398.8889 meters

Now you could try shooting at least one crew on top the tank before they get in the safety of the tank and start hunting you instead.

Or you could just buy a laser range finder (using it to range a tank might not be wise however, they might got laser detectors and in which case you would be screwed).
